_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 43 (second journey with Benjamin). Saadia-specific: v.14 'אלטאיק אלכאפי' = 'the Sufficient Power' (consistent w/ B17:1); v.30 'אללה ירופך יא אבני' = 'May God be gracious to you, my son' (Saadia's gloss for אלהים יחנך).

translations.1: And the famine was severe in the land.
translations.2: And when they had finished eating the grain-supply which they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them: 'Return — buy us a little food.'
translations.3: Judah said to him: 'The man solemnly warned us, saying, "You shall not see my face except with your brother with you."
translations.4: If you send our brother with us, we shall go down and buy food for you.
translations.5: But if you do not send him, we shall not go down — for the man said to us, "You shall not see my face except with your brother with you."'
translations.6: And Israel said: 'Why have you treated me ill, and told the man that you had still another brother?'
translations.7: They said: 'The man asked specifically about us and about our offspring, saying, "Is your father still alive? And do you have another brother?" And we told him according to the manner of his words. How could we have known that he would say, "Bring down your brother"?'
translations.8: Then Judah said to Israel his father: 'Send the boy with us; and let us arise and go, that we may live and not die — we and you and our little ones.
translations.9: I shall be his guarantor; from my hand you shall require him. If I do not bring him back to you, and set him before you, then I shall be at fault before you all my days.
translations.10: Had we not lingered, we would by now have returned twice.'
translations.11: Their father Israel said to them: 'If it is so, do this: take of the choice produce of the land in your vessels, and bring down to the man a gift — a little theriac and a little honey, carob and chestnut, terebinth, and almonds.
translations.12: And take double silver in your hand; and the silver which was returned in the mouths of your sacks, return it with you — perhaps it was an oversight.
translations.13: And take your brother; and arise, return to the man.
translations.14: And the Sufficient Power grant you mercy before him, that he may release to you your other brother along with Benjamin. And as for me, I am afraid — that I be bereaved as I have been bereaved.'
translations.15: And the men took this gift, and double silver they took with them, and Benjamin; and they arose, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
translations.16: And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to his steward: 'Bring the people into the house; slaughter a beast and prepare it — for the people shall eat with me at midday.'
translations.17: And the man did as Joseph had said; and he brought them to his house.
translations.18: And the men were afraid when they were brought to Joseph's house; and they said: 'On account of the silver which was returned in our sacks at the first, we are being brought in — that he may seek a pretext against us, and fall upon us, and take us as slaves, and seize our donkeys.'
translations.19: And they drew near to Joseph's steward, and spoke with him at the door of the house.
translations.20: And they said: 'My lord — we came down at the first to buy food.
translations.21: And it was, when we came to the lodging-place, we opened our sacks — and behold, each man's silver was in his sack, our silver by its weight; and we have brought it back with us.
translations.22: And other silver we have brought down with us to buy food. We do not know who placed our silver in our sacks.'
translations.23: He said: 'Peace to you; do not fear. Your God, and the God of your father, has granted you a treasure in your sacks; your silver came to me.' Then he brought out Simeon to them.
translations.24: And when the man brought the people into Joseph's house, he gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he put down fodder for their donkeys.
translations.25: And they prepared the gift, until Joseph came at midday — for they heard that they would eat there.
translations.26: And when Joseph came to his house, they brought him the gift which was with them into the house; and they bowed down to him upon the earth.
translations.27: And he asked them concerning their welfare, and said: 'Is your aged father, of whom you spoke, still alive? Is he well?'
translations.28: They said: 'Your servant our father is still alive, and he is well.' Then they bowed down and prostrated themselves.
translations.29: Then he lifted up his eyes, and looked upon Benjamin his brother, his mother's son; and he said: 'Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?' Then he said: 'May God be gracious to you, my son.'
translations.30: And Joseph hastened — for his compassion was stirred toward his brother — and he sought to weep; and he entered the chamber, and wept there.
translations.31: Then he washed his face, and came out, and restrained himself, and said: 'Set out the food.'
translations.32: And they set out for him alone, and for them alone, and for the Egyptians who ate with him alone — for the Egyptians cannot eat with the Hebrews at the same food, for it is an abomination to them.
translations.33: And he seated them before him — the firstborn according to his rank, and the youngest according to his rank; and the men marveled, each one with his neighbor.
translations.34: And portions were brought from before him to them; and Benjamin's portions were five times more than their portions. And they drank with him until they were drunk.
